summary: Explosive, hard-fighting anadromous gamefish that boomed off the near-collapse of the 1990s into a southern Gulf of St. Lawrence population over 900,000 strong, all spawned from one river system — the Miramichi — and now fished under a DFO slot-limit fishery from wharves, beaches, and river mouths across NB, NS, and PEI.

sections.heading: Know the Fish
sections.body_md:
Striped bass (*Morone saxatilis*) are anadromous, spawning in freshwater and doing most of their growing at sea. Identify them by 6-9 dark horizontal stripes running along a silvery body, a spiny first dorsal fin separate from the soft second dorsal, and a stout, deep-bodied shape.

The entire self-sustaining southern Gulf of St. Lawrence population spawns in one place: the tidal-fresh reach of the **Northwest Miramichi River estuary**, New Brunswick — the only confirmed successful spawning ground for this stock. Spawning happens in a brief window in late May to mid-June, concentrated over just a couple of kilometres of river, when water hits roughly 15.6-16.6°C. From near-collapse (fewer than 5,000 spawners in the late 1990s) the population rebuilt to more than 900,000 spawners by 2017, and fish from that single nursery now range every summer along the Northumberland Strait and Gulf shorelines of NB, NS, and PEI.

Note: this is a biologically separate stock from the smaller **Bay of Fundy population** (Shubenacadie/Minas Basin, NS), which has its own, much more conservative regulations (see the Nova Scotia entry below).

sections.heading: When to Go
sections.body_md:
Fish move out of Miramichi wintering grounds as ice melts (April) and are available through the tidal system and along the coast into October. Peak shore and boat action along the Northumberland Strait runs roughly **May through October**, with early season concentrated near the Miramichi and fish dispersing along NB, NS, and PEI beaches as water warms through summer.

Daily timing: DFO's fishing-hours rules (below) effectively set your day — spring/early summer is sunrise-to-sunset plus a two-hour buffer each end; summer through fall opens up to a near round-the-clock window in tidal water outside the upper Miramichi.

sources.label: DFO Gulf Region — Striped Bass Recreational Fishery in the Southern Gulf of St. Lawrence in 2026

sections.heading: Where to Find Them
sections.body_md:
- **Miramichi River estuary (NB)** — the source population; both Northwest and Southwest Miramichi hold big numbers spring and fall.
- **Hillsborough River, Charlottetown (PEI)** — a well-known top striper spot right in the capital.
- **Malpeque Bay (PEI)** — good striper and mackerel water.
- **North Shore beaches near Rustico and Cavendish, and West Point/Jacques Cartier beach (PEI)** — popular rock/beach shore fishing.
- **Northport wharf (PEI)** — locally reported wharf action.
- **Northumberland Strait shoreline generally (NB & NS)** — wharves, river mouths, and estuaries all along the strait see summer/fall striper runs as Miramichi-origin fish disperse.
- **Shubenacadie and Minas Basin area (NS)** — different, smaller Bay of Fundy stock; check the separate, stricter Maritimes Region regulations before fishing here (see Regulations).

Always confirm you have permission/access at wharves — check with the local wharf authority and use designated parking.

sections.heading: Gear
sections.body_md:
| Item | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Rod | Medium-heavy spinning rod, 7-9 ft, for casting distance off beaches/wharves and handling fish up to the 65 cm max slot. |
| Reel | Spinning reel with a strong, smooth drag and 150+ yards of 15-20 lb braid. |
| Terminal tackle | Single barbless hooks are mandatory — swap out trebles on hard baits for single inline hooks. |
| Lures/bait | Soft plastic paddletails and swimbaits, topwater poppers at dawn/dusk, and fresh-cut mackerel or gaspereau chunk bait on bottom rigs. |
| Extras | Long-handled net or lip-grip tool, tape measure (the 50-65 cm slot is enforced by law), pliers for quick hook removal. |

sections.heading: Technique
sections.body_md:
**Shore/wharf casting:** Cast paddletail swimbaits or spoons across the current and let them swing, retrieving with a steady swim or short pumps — stripers often hold on current seams near pilings, river mouths, and drop-offs adjacent to wharves.

**Topwater:** Dawn and dusk, work poppers or walk-the-dog style plugs over shallow flats and sandbars where bass are pushing bait.

**Bait fishing:** Fresh-cut mackerel or gaspereau on a simple bottom rig (egg sinker above a swivel, leader, single barbless hook) fished in current seams or river-mouth holes is a proven, low-effort producer, especially for bigger fish.

**Measure before you decide to keep one** — the 50-65 cm slot is unforgiving and DFO enforces it; a fish outside that window must go back immediately.

sources.label: DFO Gulf Region — Striped Bass Recreational Fishery in the Southern Gulf of St. Lawrence in 2026

sections.heading: Handling & Release
sections.body_md:
- Fish outside the 50-65 cm slot, and anything beyond your daily/possession limit of 4, must be released immediately.
- Support the fish horizontally with wet hands; avoid squeezing the belly or holding by the eyes/gills.
- Use single barbless hooks (legally required) to speed unhooking and cut handling time.
- If bleeding heavily from deep hooking, consider it a mortality risk and count it against your limit rather than trying to release a fish unlikely to survive.
- Never fish or handle striped bass in the Northwest Miramichi spawning closure zone when it's posted (a roughly 9.8 km stretch that can close for up to 10 days during peak spawning).

sources.label: DFO Gulf Region — Striped Bass Recreational Fishery in the Southern Gulf of St. Lawrence in 2026

sections.heading: Conservation & Consumption Notes
sections.body_md:
The southern Gulf population's recovery from under 5,000 spawners in the late 1990s to over 900,000 by 2017 is a genuine conservation success story, driven directly by tight recreational and commercial controls — which is exactly why the slot limit, hook restrictions, and Miramichi spawning closure exist and are actively enforced. Fish within the slot cook up well and there's no widespread consumption advisory for this species in the region, but treat the Miramichi spawning grounds and closure notices as non-negotiable: this is the one river that sustains the entire regional fishery.

The separate Bay of Fundy (Shubenacadie/Minas Basin) stock is far smaller and managed far more conservatively by DFO Maritimes Region — don't assume Gulf Region rules apply there.
